claims.text: HFrEF: reduces all-cause mortality and should be considered in all HFrEF patients;
claims.quote: In patients with HFrEF, the ARNI sacubitril/valsartan reduces all-cause mortality and should be considered in all patients with HFrEF (1, 2).

claims.text: preferred over an ACE inhibitor or ARB if tolerated, with early switching supported even in hospital.
claims.quote: It is preferred over an ACE inhibitor or ARB if tolerated, and evidence supports early transition of patients from an ACE inhibitor or ARB to ARNI, even in the hospital setting.

claims.text: Start 49/51 mg BID if previously on an ACE inhibitor or ARB; 24/26 mg BID if on a low dose, ACE-I/ARB-naive, or with low/borderline BP.
claims.quote: The starting dose of sacubitril/valsartan is 49/51 mg orally twice a day for patients previously taking an ACE inhibitor or ARB, and 24/26 mg for patients previously taking a low dose of an ACE inhibitor or ARB (eg, ≤ 10 mg enalapril daily) or in those patients who have not taken an ACE inhibitor or an ARB or who have low or borderline blood pressure.

claims.text: Double after 2 to 4 weeks to the target 97/103 mg BID as tolerated.
claims.quote: Double the dose of ENTRESTO after 2 to 4 weeks to the target maintenance dose of 97/103 mg twice daily, as tolerated by the patient.

claims.text: Patients on an ARB can switch with no washout.
claims.quote: Patients previously taking an ARB can simply switch to sacubitril/valsartan without a washout period.

claims.text: K-sparing diuretics, K supplements or K-containing salt substitutes may raise serum K;
claims.quote: As with other drugs that block angiotensin II or its effects, concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium may lead to increases in serum potassium [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)] .

claims.text: lithium toxicity has been reported with ARBs, so monitor lithium levels.
claims.quote: Increases in serum lithium concentrations and lithium toxicity have been reported during concomitant administration of lithium with angiotensin II receptor antagonists. Monitor serum lithium levels during concomitant use with ENTRESTO.

claims.text: Overdose: hypotension is the most likely result; treat symptomatically.
claims.quote: Hypotension is the most likely result of overdosage due to the blood pressure lowering effects of ENTRESTO. Symptomatic treatment should be provided.
